name: accept-approved-by
description: A refund request under alice's root grant, with an approved_by claim with covers proven by her approval, the approval.request it answers and the pcm.grant decision that request names: the approval issued the message's root grant, so it covers the request; replay checked.

name: accept-tests-passed-t2
description: The accept message plus tests_passed proven by a result the tool executor wrote (T2).

name: accept-unproven-no-evidence
description: The accept message plus a tests_passed claim with no evidence.

name: accept-unproven-t1-result
description: tests_passed whose only result is the agent's own report (T1).

name: accept-unproven-unplaced-tool
description: tests_passed run by the executor through mcp:ci/run, a tool the placement table does not list as shell.

name: reject-strict-required-unproven
description: strict: the schema requires approved_by and the claim has no evidence.

name: reject-envelope-extra-field
description: A field the envelope does not have, added after signing.

name: reject-envelope-pcm-false
description: pcm set to false after signing: it must be the integer 0.

name: reject-forged-signature
description: amount changed after signing, signature kept.

name: reject-unpinned-key
description: A valid message; trust pins only another log's key.

name: reject-grant-signature-as-message
description: The message body signed for the grant purpose (pcm.grant.v0) with the test log key, offline.

name: reject-unknown-schema
description: A valid refund.quote; the receiver has only the refund.request schema.

name: reject-schema-extra-field
description: Args with an arg the schema does not list.

name: reject-schema-int-as-string
description: Args with order as the string "81".

name: reject-schema-bool-as-int
description: Args with order as true, a bool for an int field.

name: reject-schema-money-over-max
description: Args with amount 1000001, over the max 1000000.

name: reject-replay-duplicate-nonce
description: The receiver already took this message: its nonce was seen.

name: reject-replay-outside-window
description: Checked 600 s after it was signed, with a 300 s window.

name: reject-replay-before-started
description: Signed 1 s before the receiver started.

name: reject-wrong-recipient
description: Addressed to uid:990102, checked by uid:990103.

name: reject-replay-no-real-time
description: ts set to month 13 and re-signed with the test log key (the signer takes ts from its clock): the TS pattern lets it through, the replay check refuses it.

name: reject-grant-amount-over-caveat
description: amount 50000 under a grant of amount <= 20000.

name: reject-grant-expired
description: Signed after its root grant expired (a grant made to expire in 3 s).

name: reject-grant-cross-tenant
description: A root grant carol approved in a run of tenant acme, used by a sender in tenant default.

name: reject-grant-root-by-agent
description: The root grant's issuer kind edited to agent and re-signed with the test log key (the signer issues root grants only from a person's approval).

name: reject-grant-subject-not-sender
description: A root grant for uid:990102, sent by uid:990101.

name: accept-delegation-narrowing
description: Two steps: alice's delegable grant to A (amount <= 20000), A's child to B (amount <= 15000); B asks for 12000.

name: reject-delegation-over-child-cap
description: The same chain; B asks for 18000, within the root's cap but over the child's.

name: reject-grant-widening-child
description: A's child to B raises the cap to 30000; the signer refuses it, so it is the real child edited and re-signed with the test log key.

name: reject-grant-widen-and-tighten-child
description: A's child to B raises the cap to 30000 and adds amount >= 100; the signer refuses it, so it is the real child edited and re-signed with the test log key.

name: reject-grant-missing-caveat-child
description: A's child to B drops order == 81; the signer refuses it, so it is the real child edited and re-signed with the test log key.

name: reject-grant-below-non-delegable
description: A child below alice's grant that can't be passed on; the signer refuses it, so it is the real child edited and re-signed with the test log key under the non-delegable root.

name: reject-grant-broken-parent
description: A real child placed under another real root, so its parent hash names another grant.

name: reject-claim-changed-record-hash
description: approved_by whose first record's hash has one hex digit changed.

name: reject-claim-cut-proof
description: approved_by whose first record's inclusion proof lost its last hash.

name: reject-claim-unpinned-log-note
description: approved_by under a checkpoint note of a log trust does not pin.

name: reject-claim-evidence-from-another-log
description: approved_by with alice's approval records of the test log as evidence, sent by uid:990101 of the other log from a run it registered there under the run id of A's run (run ids are the client's, unique per log only), so the records are of the sender's run id and tenant; trust pins both logs: the note is not of the log that signed the message.

name: reject-grant-from-another-log
description: A root grant alice approved on the other log, for uid:990101 there, sent by uid:990101 of the test log; trust pins both logs. Identities are names inside one log: the grant is not this sender's.

name: accept-replay-same-agent-other-log
description: The receiver first took a message from uid:990101 of the other log with the nonce of this one (re-signed with the other log's test key); trust pins both logs. A sender is the pair (public key, agent), so uid:990101 of the test log is another sender and its nonce is new.

name: reject-claim-proof-non-canonical-base64
description: approved_by whose first record's first proof entry has an unused bit of its last base64 character set: the same 32 bytes, but only canonical base64 is taken.

name: reject-claim-witnesses-required-unmet
description: approved_by under a note with no cosignature; trust requires one witness.

name: reject-claim-wrong-person
description: approved_by naming bob; the approval record is alice's.

name: reject-claim-approval-of-another-call
description: approved_by of call grant-2, with alice's approval of grant-1 as evidence.

name: reject-claim-pytest-or-true
description: tests_passed of `pytest ... || true`, run by the executor (T2): its status is not the tests'.

name: reject-claim-approved-by-unmapped-identity
description: approved_by naming uid:990009, an approver no person in the signer's approvals configuration maps to, with its approval, request and decision as evidence: only a person's name proves it.

name: reject-claim-approved-by-rejected-answer
description: approved_by of call grant-rejected, with alice's answer, the request and the decision as evidence: she answered reject, which approves nothing.

name: reject-claim-approved-by-without-decision
description: approved_by whose evidence holds alice's approval and the approval.request it answers, but not the policy.decision the request names: the call id is the agent's own name for the call, so without its decision nothing says what was approved.

name: accept-approved-by-opened-args
description: approved_by of call pay-1, without covers, on a refund.quote, which needs no claim. The agent decided pay-1 twice: a pay of 50000, then a read_file of /etc/motd. alice approved the read_file, and the evidence opens its decision: the result's approved names the read_file and its args, whatever the call id says.

name: reject-claim-record-listed-twice
description: approved_by whose evidence lists the opened read_file decision of pay-1 twice: evidence that lists a record twice fails, so a decision listed opened and unopened can't make what was approved depend on the order of the records.

name: reject-claim-approved-by-other-decision
description: approved_by of call pay-1, which the agent decided twice: a pay of 50000, then a read_file of /etc/motd. alice approved the read_file (the approval.request names its decision), and the evidence holds the pay decision with that request and approval: an approval is of the decision its request names, not of every decision of the call id.

name: reject-claim-approved-by-self-approval
description: approved_by erin, sent by her own agent's run (uid:990011, which the approvals configuration maps to erin too), with her approval of its call, the request and the decision as evidence; the signer allows self-approval, so it recorded the answer with self_approved true: a person approving her own agent's call is no independent approval.

name: reject-claim-evidence-from-another-run
description: approved_by with alice's approval records as evidence, sent by another run of the same agent: evidence must come from the sender's own run.

name: reject-claim-evidence-from-another-tenant
description: approved_by with alice's approval records as evidence, sent by uid:990107 of tenant acme from a run it registered under the run id of A's run (a client picks its run id): the records are of tenant default, so they are not the sender's.

name: accept-witnessed
description: approved_by under a note cosigned by the pinned witness; trust requires one witness.

name: reject-claim-malformed-unpinned-note-line
description: approved_by under a note with an extra signature line of a key trust does not pin, whose signature is 3 bytes: a malformed line fails the note even when its key is not pinned.

name: reject-claim-record-not-an-event
description: approved_by whose approval record has the number 5 as its prev_hash, which no claim checker reads, under a checkpoint the test log key signs offline over the edited record: a record that is no valid tracekit.event.v2 event fails.

name: reject-claim-approved-by-agent-approver
description: approved_by whose evidence is alice's approval, its request and decision, with approver_kind agent added to the approval, under a checkpoint the test log key signs offline over the edited records (an honest signer writes no person on an agent approver's answer): an agent approver's answer proves no person's approval.

name: reject-claim-approved-by-request-of-another-approval
description: approved_by whose evidence is alice's approval, its request and decision, with the request's approval_id changed to apr-other, so no request in the evidence names the approval, under a checkpoint the test log key signs offline over the edited records.

name: reject-claim-approved-by-decision-of-another-call
description: approved_by whose evidence is alice's approval, its request and decision, with the decision's tool_use_id changed to grant-other, so the decision the request names is not of the claimed call, under a checkpoint the test log key signs offline over the edited records.

name: reject-claim-approved-by-decision-without-tool
description: approved_by whose evidence is alice's approval, its request and decision, with the decision's tool removed, so nothing says what was approved, under a checkpoint the test log key signs offline over the edited records.

name: reject-claim-approved-by-two-decisions
description: approved_by of call pay-1 whose evidence holds alice's approval of the read_file decision with its request, and a second approval by alice of pay-1 with a request naming the pay decision, under a checkpoint the test log key signs offline (a signer keeps one approval per call): approvals of the call that name different decisions fail the claim, whatever the order of the records.

name: reject-claim-approved-by-args-true-and-1
description: approved_by of call pay-2, which the agent decided twice, a pay of {"amount": true} and a pay of {"amount": 1}, whose evidence opens both decisions and holds alice's approval of the second with its request, and a second approval by alice of pay-2 with a request naming the first, under a checkpoint the test log key signs offline: the two pairs of tool and args differ in JCS, though Python's == takes them as equal, so the approvals name different decisions and the claim fails.

name: reject-claim-approved-by-request-names-two-decisions
description: approved_by of call pay-1 whose evidence holds alice's approval, its request and the read_file decision, plus a second approval.request of the same approval naming the pay decision (not in the evidence), under a checkpoint the test log key signs offline: requests of one approval that name two decisions fail the claim.

name: reject-claim-witness-key-in-logs
description: approved_by with trust pinning the witness's cosignature key in logs, next to the test log key: a key in logs that is no Ed25519 or hybrid log key fails the note.

name: reject-claim-tests-passed-malformed-no-evidence
description: tests_passed of `pytest ... || true` with no evidence: a suite that is no test command is malformed, so the claim fails without evidence too.

name: reject-claim-file-written-relative-no-evidence
description: file_written of the relative path work/report.txt with no evidence: the claim is malformed, so it fails without evidence too.

name: accept-approved-by-covers-direct
description: A refund.pay request of 12000, whose schema needs approved_by and names the tool pay, with an approved_by claim citing alice's approval of a pay of the request's args, opened: the tool the schema names, and the intent's args.

name: accept-unproven-approved-by-covers-not-opened
description: A refund.pay request of 12000, whose schema needs approved_by and names the tool pay, with an approved_by claim citing alice's approval of a pay whose decision the evidence does not open, so the verifier can't tell whether its args are the request's.

name: accept-unproven-approved-by-covers-schema-without-tool
description: A refund.pay request of 12000, whose schema needs approved_by and names no tool, with an approved_by claim citing alice's approval of a pay of the request's args, opened: the schema names no tool, so the verifier can't tell whether the approval covers the request.

name: reject-claim-approved-by-covers-other-args
description: A refund.pay request of 12000, whose schema needs approved_by and names the tool pay, with an approved_by claim citing alice's approval of a pay of 500, opened, cited for a pay of 12000.

name: reject-claim-approved-by-covers-other-tool
description: A refund.pay request of 12000, whose schema needs approved_by and names the tool pay, with an approved_by claim citing alice's approval of a read_file, not opened: the decision's tool is in the record, so it fails unopened too.

name: accept-unproven-approved-by-required-without-covers
description: A refund.pay request of 12000, whose schema needs approved_by and names the tool pay, with an approved_by claim citing alice's approval of a pay of 500, opened, cited for a pay of 12000 without covers: the claim is proven, as alice approved that call, but meets the schema's need only with covers.

name: reject-claim-approved-by-covers-args-true-and-1
description: A refund.pay request of 12000 for order 1, whose schema needs approved_by and names the tool pay, with an approved_by claim with covers citing alice's approval of a pay for order true, opened: true and 1 differ in JCS, though Python's == takes them as equal, so the approval does not cover the request.

name: accept-approved-by-covers-grant
description: A refund under alice's root grant, whose schema names the tool pay, with an approved_by claim with covers citing her approval of the pcm.grant call that issued the root grant: the grant path holds whatever tool the schema names.

name: reject-claim-approved-by-covers-grant-not-root
description: A refund request under alice's root grant of call grant-1, with an approved_by claim with covers citing her approval of call grant-b, a pcm.grant call that issued another grant: a pcm.grant approval covers only the requests under the grant it issued.

name: reject-claim-bash-c
description: tests_passed of `bash -c 'pytest || true'`, run by the executor (T2): bash is not a test runner.

name: reject-claim-tests-passed-comment
description: tests_passed of `pytest -q tests/test_refund.py # || true`, run by the executor (T2): a suite may hold no `#`, even where the shell reads a comment, so it is no test command.

name: reject-claim-hash-inside-word
description: tests_passed of `pytest -q tests/test_refund.py#|| true`, run by the executor (T2): a `#` inside a word starts no comment, so the shell runs `|| true`, so it is no test command.

name: reject-claim-tests-passed-background
description: tests_passed of `pytest -q tests/test_refund.py &`, run by the executor (T2): the shell runs the tests in the background and exits 0 whatever they do, so it is no test command.

name: reject-claim-tests-passed-ansi-c-quote
description: tests_passed of `pytest $'\'';true #'`, run by the executor (T2): sh reads `$'\''` as one quote and runs `true`, where Python's shlex reads one word, so it is no test command.

name: reject-claim-tests-passed-unbalanced-quote
description: tests_passed of `pytest -q 'tests/test_refund.py`, run by the executor (T2): its quotes don't balance, so it is no test command.

name: reject-claim-tests-passed-dot-slash
description: tests_passed of `./pytest -q`, run by the executor (T2): the program must be the runner's bare name, not a file of that name, so it is no test command.

name: reject-claim-tests-passed-runner-path
description: tests_passed of `.venv/bin/pytest -q`, run by the executor (T2): the program must be the runner's bare name, so it is no test command.

name: reject-claim-tests-passed-co
description: tests_passed of `pytest --co -q`, run by the executor (T2): --co is a flag with which a runner runs no tests, or a prefix of one, so it is no test command.

name: reject-claim-tests-passed-collect-only
description: tests_passed of `pytest --collect-only -q`, run by the executor (T2): --collect-only is a flag with which a runner runs no tests, or a prefix of one, so it is no test command.

name: reject-claim-tests-passed-help
description: tests_passed of `pytest --help -q`, run by the executor (T2): --help is a flag with which a runner runs no tests, or a prefix of one, so it is no test command.

name: reject-claim-tests-passed-h
description: tests_passed of `pytest -h -q`, run by the executor (T2): -h is a flag with which a runner runs no tests, or a prefix of one, so it is no test command.

name: reject-claim-tests-passed-version
description: tests_passed of `pytest --version -q`, run by the executor (T2): --version is a flag with which a runner runs no tests, or a prefix of one, so it is no test command.

name: reject-claim-tests-passed-V
description: tests_passed of `pytest -V -q`, run by the executor (T2): -V is a flag with which a runner runs no tests, or a prefix of one, so it is no test command.

name: reject-claim-tests-passed-he
description: tests_passed of `pytest --he -q`, run by the executor (T2): --he is a flag with which a runner runs no tests, or a prefix of one, so it is no test command.

name: reject-claim-tests-passed-wrapper
description: tests_passed of `uv run pytest -q`, run by the executor (T2): a wrapper in front is not in the list of test commands.

name: accept-tests-passed-npm-test
description: tests_passed of `npm test`, run by the executor (T2).

name: accept-tests-passed-python-m-pytest
description: tests_passed of `python3 -m pytest -q`, run by the executor (T2).

name: reject-claim-tests-failed
description: tests_passed whose T2 result is an error.

name: reject-claim-tests-passed-denied-call
description: tests_passed of `pytest -q tests/test_denied.py`, whose policy.decision is deny; the executor then reported the call ran and succeeded (T2): a denied decision matches no call.

name: reject-claim-salt-without-args
description: tests_passed whose decision record carries its salt but not its args.

name: reject-claim-opening-wrong-args
description: tests_passed whose opening carries other args than the decision committed to.

name: reject-claim-decision-without-id
description: tests_passed whose policy.decision and tool.result records both lost data.decision_id, under a checkpoint the test log key signs offline over the edited records: a decision without its id matches no call, though the two still pair by their missing ids.

name: accept-file-written
description: file_written of /work/report.txt by a Write of /work/report.txt the executor ran (T2), with the SHA-256 of the content written.

name: reject-claim-file-written-wrong-digest
description: file_written of /work/report.txt by a Write of /work/report.txt the executor ran (T2), with another digest than the content's.

name: reject-claim-file-written-dotdot
description: file_written of /work/../work/report.txt by a Write of /work/report.txt the executor ran (T2), naming the path with `..`, which fails.

name: reject-claim-file-written-not-write-tool
description: file_written of /work/report.txt by an Edit of /work/report.txt the executor ran (T2), whose args carry the whole content with that digest: only the tool Write writes a file, whatever the args of another tool hold.

name: reject-claim-file-written-relative
description: file_written of work/report.txt by a Write of work/report.txt the executor ran (T2): the paths are equal, but a relative claim is malformed, so it fails.

name: accept-unproven-file-written-relative-call
description: file_written of /work/report.txt by a Write of report.txt the executor ran (T2): the record doesn't hold the working directory, so the relative path may name this file or another.

name: reject-claim-file-written-backslash
description: file_written of /work/report.txt by a Write of /work\report.txt the executor ran (T2): a path that starts with / is read by POSIX rules, where `\` is part of a name, so the call wrote the file `work\report.txt` in /.

name: accept-unproven-file-written-drive-separators
description: file_written of C:\work\report.txt by a Write of C:/work/report.txt the executor ran (T2): the two are one file on Windows, but the record doesn't say which system ran the call, and on POSIX C:/work/report.txt is a relative path.

name: accept-file-written-drive-path
description: file_written of C:\work\report.txt by a Write of C:\work\report.txt the executor ran (T2): a drive path is proven by a call of the claim's own string.

name: accept-reached-host-observed
description: reached_host proven by the effect.observed record an egress observer reported to the signer: a minute with one connection to the host.

name: accept-unproven-reached-host-no-connection
description: reached_host api.example.com by an egress observer's minute of the run's traffic to the host with connections 0 (its connect failed): the run tried the host, nothing says it reached it.

name: accept-unproven-reached-host-sensor-connect
description: reached_host api.example.com by a kernel sensor's (Tetragon's) record that a process of the run called connect to the host: the attempt, not an opened connection.

name: reject-claim-reached-host-denied-connect
description: reached_host api.example.com by a kernel sensor import's connect of the run to the host, marked denied (the sensor blocked it): a denied connect reaches nothing, and nothing else in the evidence says the run reached the host.

name: accept-unproven-reached-host-unreadable-claim
description: reached_host of a..example with the observed evidence: a host with an empty label won't parse, so the claim is unproven.

name: accept-unproven-reached-host-claim-not-quad
description: reached_host of 0127.0.0.1 with the observed evidence: an IPv4 address not written as a dotted quad won't parse, and the detail says how to write it.

name: accept-reached-host-http
description: reached_host api.example.com by a WebFetch of https://API.Example.COM:8443/v1/refunds the executor ran (T2): the host is read lower case, without the port.

name: accept-reached-host-claim-port
description: reached_host api.example.com:443 by a WebFetch of https://api.example.com/v1/refunds the executor ran (T2): a port in the claim is ignored too.

name: accept-reached-host-trailing-dot
description: reached_host api.example.com by a WebFetch of https://api.example.com./v1/refunds the executor ran (T2): the host loses its one trailing dot.

name: accept-reached-host-dotted-quad
description: reached_host 10.0.0.1 by a WebFetch of http://10.0.0.1:8080/health the executor ran (T2): an IPv4 address written as four decimal numbers 0-255 without leading zeros, 0 itself among them.

name: accept-unproven-reached-host-ipv4-leading-zero
description: reached_host 87.0.0.1 by a WebFetch of http://0127.0.0.1/ok the executor ran (T2): inet_aton reads 0127 as octal, 87, where macOS's resolver reads it as decimal and connects to 127.0.0.1: an IPv4 address not written as a dotted quad won't parse.

name: accept-unproven-reached-host-short-ipv4
description: reached_host 127.0.0.1 by a WebFetch of http://127.1/health the executor ran (T2): inet_aton reads 127.1 as 127.0.0.1, but a host whose last label is a number counts only as a dotted quad.

name: accept-unproven-reached-host-hex-ipv4
description: reached_host 127.0.0.1 by a WebFetch of http://0x7f.0.0.1/ the executor ran (T2): a hex label, which resolvers read apart, so it won't parse.

name: accept-unproven-reached-host-ipv4-number
description: reached_host 127.0.0.1 by a WebFetch of http://2130706433/ the executor ran (T2): one number, 127.0.0.1 to inet_aton, is no dotted quad, so it won't parse.

name: accept-reached-host-a-label
description: reached_host xn--bcher-kva.example by a WebFetch of https://XN--BCHER-KVA.Example/ the executor ran (T2): an xn-- label is compared as written, in lower case: a name in another script is fetched and claimed in its A-label form.

name: accept-reached-host-ipv4-mapped
description: reached_host 1.2.3.4 by a WebFetch of http://[::ffff:1.2.3.4]/ the executor ran (T2): an IPv4-mapped IPv6 address is compared as the IPv4 address inside.

name: accept-reached-host-nat64
description: reached_host 1.2.3.4 by a WebFetch of http://[64:ff9b::102:304]/ the executor ran (T2): a NAT64 IPv6 address (64:ff9b::/96) is compared as the IPv4 address inside.

name: accept-unproven-reached-host-label-character
description: reached_host api.example.com by a WebFetch of http://a*b.example/ the executor ran (T2): a label holds only a-z, 0-9, `_` and `-`, so the host a*b.example won't parse, though a browser reads it: the claim is unproven, not failed.

name: accept-unproven-reached-host-two-trailing-dots
description: reached_host a.example by a WebFetch of http://a.example../ the executor ran (T2): a host loses one trailing dot only, so a.example. has an empty label and won't parse.

name: accept-unproven-reached-host-browser-brackets
description: reached_host h.com by a WebFetch of http:\\[h.com]/ the executor ran (T2): the URL has no authority, and the browser reading is [h.com], which starts with `[` and is no IPv6 address in brackets, so it won't parse.

name: accept-unproven-reached-host-not-ipv6
description: reached_host api.example.com by a WebFetch of http:\\[::g]/ the executor ran (T2): the browser reading [::g] holds a `:` and is no IPv6 address, so the host won't parse: the reading is not left out, as an empty one is, which would leave no host and fail the claim.

name: accept-unproven-reached-host-ipv6-leading-zero-backslash
description: reached_host 1.2.3.4 by a WebFetch of http:\\[::ffff:01.2.3.4]/ the executor ran (T2): a leading zero in the dotted quad of the browser reading [::ffff:01.2.3.4], and no authority for the bracket rule to refuse: the canonical form refuses it, so a verifier whose IPv6 parser reads 01 as 1 doesn't prove 1.2.3.4.

name: accept-unproven-reached-host-idn
description: reached_host xn--bcher-kva.example by a WebFetch of http://bücher.example/ the executor ran (T2): IDNA 2003 and UTS 46 both read the name as xn--bcher-kva.example, but hosts are compared in ASCII only: a URL with a character outside printable ASCII won't parse.

name: reject-claim-reached-host-other-host
description: reached_host api.example.org by a WebFetch of https://api.example.com/v1/refunds the executor ran (T2): another host.

name: accept-unproven-reached-host-bracket
description: reached_host good.com by a WebFetch of http://[x]@good.com/ the executor ran (T2): a bracket in the user info: the bracket rule refuses the URL, so its host won't parse.

name: accept-unproven-reached-host-bracket-ipv6-userinfo
description: reached_host api.example.com by a WebFetch of http://[::1]@api.example.com/ the executor ran (T2): a bracketed IPv6 address in the user info: the bracket rule refuses it, though one of urlsplit's bracket checks passes it and reads api.example.com.

name: accept-unproven-reached-host-bracket-other-host
description: reached_host api.example.com by a WebFetch of http://[::1]@evil.example/ the executor ran (T2): a bracketed IPv6 address in the user info before another host: the bracket rule refuses it, so the claim is unproven, not failed.

name: accept-unproven-reached-host-two-brackets
description: reached_host ::1 by a WebFetch of http://[zz]@[::1]/ the executor ran (T2): two pairs of brackets: the bracket rule takes only one, around the host, so it refuses this though a browser reaches [::1].

name: accept-unproven-reached-host-bracket-trailing
description: reached_host ::1 by a WebFetch of http://[::1]x/ the executor ran (T2): text after the `]` that is no port: the bracket rule refuses it.

name: accept-unproven-reached-host-bracket-not-host
description: reached_host x by a WebFetch of http://[@x::1]/ the executor ran (T2): the `[` is in the user info, not at the start of the host after the `@`: the bracket rule refuses it, where a reader without urlsplit's bracket check reads the host x.

name: accept-unproven-reached-host-ambiguous
description: reached_host b.example by a WebFetch of http://a.example\@b.example/ the executor ran (T2): a browser reads the host a.example and Python's urllib b.example, so it won't parse.

name: accept-unproven-reached-host-deviation
description: reached_host fass.example by a WebFetch of http://faß.example/ the executor ran (T2): IDNA 2003 maps the sharp s to ss, so a verifier that read the name by it would prove fass.example, where a browser reaches xn--fa-hia.example: a URL with a character outside printable ASCII won't parse.

name: accept-unproven-reached-host-mapped-to-nothing
description: reached_host example.com by a WebFetch of http://exa᠆mple.com/ the executor ran (T2): IDNA 2003 maps U+1806 to nothing, so a verifier that read the name by it would prove example.com, where UTS 46 refuses the name: a URL with a character outside printable ASCII won't parse.

name: accept-unproven-reached-host-tab-in-escape
description: reached_host fass.example by a WebFetch of http://fa%C3	%9F.example/ the executor ran (T2): a tab inside a percent-escape, which URL readers drop, leaving fa%C3%9F.example, a sharp s once decoded: a URL with a character outside printable ASCII won't parse.

name: accept-unproven-reached-host-leading-space
description: reached_host api.example.com by a WebFetch of  https://api.example.com/v1/refunds the executor ran (T2): a leading space, which some URL readers strip and others keep: a URL with a character outside printable ASCII won't parse.

name: accept-unproven-reached-host-non-ascii-path
description: reached_host api.example.com by a WebFetch of https://api.example.com/café the executor ran (T2): a character outside printable ASCII in the path: anywhere in the URL, it makes the host one that won't parse.

name: accept-unproven-reached-host-fullwidth-ipv6
description: reached_host ::1 by a WebFetch of http://[::１]/ the executor ran (T2): a fullwidth digit one in the brackets, which NFKC makes ::1: a URL with a character outside printable ASCII won't parse.

name: accept-unproven-reached-host-ipv6-leading-zero
description: reached_host 1.2.3.4 by a WebFetch of http://[::ffff:01.2.3.4]/ the executor ran (T2): a leading zero in the IPv6 address's dotted quad, which some IPv6 parsers read as 1.2.3.4 and others refuse: it is no IPv6 address, so the bracket rule refuses the URL.

name: accept-unproven-reached-host-ipv6-leading-zero-later-octet
description: reached_host 1.2.3.4 by a WebFetch of http://[::ffff:1.2.03.4]/ the executor ran (T2): a leading zero in a later part of the IPv6 address's dotted quad: it is no IPv6 address either, so the bracket rule refuses the URL.

name: accept-unproven-reached-host-bracket-no-host
description: reached_host api.example.com by a WebFetch of http://[::1]@/ the executor ran (T2): a bracketed IPv6 address in the user info and no host after it: the bracket rule refuses the URL before anything else reads it, so the claim is unproven, not failed, whatever urlsplit's own bracket check.

name: reject-claim-reached-host-file-url
description: reached_host api.example.com by a WebFetch of file://api.example.com/x the executor ran (T2): a file: URL has no host a browser reads.

name: accept-unproven-reached-host-claim-no-host
description: reached_host :80 by a WebFetch of file:///x the executor ran (T2): the claim :80 is a port and no host, so it won't parse, rather than match the no host of a file: URL.

name: accept-unproven-reached-host-blob
description: reached_host api.example.com by a WebFetch of blob:https://api.example.com/x the executor ran (T2): a browser's address bar reads the URL inside blob:, where WHATWG URL reads no host, so it won't parse.

name: accept-unproven-reached-host-relative-path
description: reached_host api.example.com by a WebFetch of /api.example.com/v1/refunds the executor ran (T2): a URL with no scheme that starts with one slash, which a client given a base URL reads as a path on the base's host, where an address bar reads api.example.com: it won't parse.

name: accept-unproven-reached-host-percent
description: reached_host api.example.com by a WebFetch of http://%61pi.example.com/ the executor ran (T2): %61 is a, but a host is never percent-decoded: a host with a `%` won't parse.

name: accept-unproven-reached-host-nul
description: reached_host api.example.com by a WebFetch of http://api.example.com%00.evil/ the executor ran (T2): a host with a `%` won't parse, so the NUL that %00 escapes can't cut it short.

name: accept-unproven-reached-host-claim-bad-port
description: reached_host of api.example.com:abc with the observed evidence: a port must be 1 to 5 digits, so the claim won't parse.

name: reject-claim-reached-host-too-long
description: reached_host of a 200-character host: a claim's host is an id, at most 128 characters.

name: reject-sig-non-canonical-base64
description: sig.sig with an unused bit of its last base64 character set: the same 64 bytes, but only canonical base64 is taken, so a signature has one text form.

name: reject-small-order-key
description: trust pins a key that is the identity point (small order). The signature R = identity, S = 0 holds for any message under the plain equation; a verifier must refuse the key.

name: accept-identity-line-break-chars
description: to.agent holds a carriage return and U+2028: an identity's subject is any character but a line feed.

name: accept-jcs-payload
description: A data payload with floats, a non-ASCII key, a key outside the BMP that sorts before U+E000 by UTF-16 code units, controls and U+2028: the signature verifies only with exact RFC 8785.

name: bad-input-number-past-double
description: A valid refund.quote as JSON text with `"payload": {"kind": "data", "data": {"n": 1e400}}` added after signing: 1e400 rounds to no finite IEEE 754 double, so the text doesn't parse and the verifier refuses it before any check, where one that read it as infinity would fail the signature instead.

name: reject-replay-floor-arrival-order
description: per_sender 1, no window: the receiver took the 3rd, then the 1st message, so the 3rd left first and raised the floor to its time; the 2nd is older than the floor.

name: accept-replay-misaddressed-spends-no-nonce
description: The receiver uid:990102 first got this message with the same sender, ts and nonce, re-signed with the test log key but addressed to uid:990103: a message for another receiver spends no nonce here, so this one is fresh.

name: accept-replay-schema-rejected-spends-no-nonce
description: The receiver first got this message with the same sender, ts and nonce, re-signed with the test log key but with order as the string "81", which its schema refuses: a message rejected for its schema spends no nonce, so this one is fresh.

name: reject-replay-grant-failure-spends-nonce
description: The receiver first got a message of the same sender with this nonce whose grant check failed (amount 50000 over the cap of 20000); this valid one carries that nonce, re-signed with the test log key: a message rejected for its grants spends its nonce, so this one is a replay.

name: accept-skipped-replay-and-recipient
description: A valid refund.quote checked with no replay state and no receiver identity (me null), as an audit: the result names both checks in skipped.

name: accept-schema-field-types
description: A string, id, enum, bool and time field, and an optional field left out.

name: reject-schema-field-types
description: Each field of the same schema broken: a title of 81 characters, a code the pattern refuses, a level not in the enum, 0 for a bool, a time without microseconds, an optional field too long.

name: reject-grant-needed
description: refund.request needs a grant (grant: true); the message has none.

name: reject-grant-tampered
description: alice's root grant, with delegable set to true after signing.

name: reject-grant-unpinned-key
description: alice's root grant, signed by the other log, which trust does not pin.

name: reject-grant-issuer-is-subject
description: alice's root grant, with its issuer id edited to its subject, re-signed with the test log key.

name: reject-grant-bad-caveat
description: alice's root grant, with an `in` caveat on a money field, re-signed with the test log key.

name: reject-grant-other-intent
description: A root grant for refund.quote, sent with a refund.request.

name: accept-delegation-less-than
description: A's child to B has amount < 20001, which narrows amount <= 20000.

name: reject-grant-child-outlives-parent
description: A's child to B expires 60 s after its parent; the signer refuses it, so it is the real child edited and re-signed with the test log key.

name: reject-grant-child-wrong-issuer
description: A's child to B names uid:990107, not the parent's subject, as its issuer; the signer refuses it, so it is the real child edited and re-signed with the test log key.

name: reject-grant-root-with-parent
description: alice's root grant with its parent set to another grant's hash, re-signed with the test log key.

name: reject-grant-root-without-person
description: alice's root grant with issuer.person removed (the signer names the person on every root grant), re-signed with the test log key.

name: accept-grant-expires-at-ts
description: A message whose ts is its root grant's expires_at, re-signed with the test log key (the signer takes ts from its clock): a grant still holds at its expires_at.

name: reject-grant-caveat-string-for-int
description: A root grant alice approved with order == "81", the string "81" for the int field order: nothing is converted, so a caveat's value of another JSON type than its field's is no valid caveat, and no args satisfy it.

name: reject-grant-caveat-bool-for-int
description: A root grant alice approved with order == true, a bool for the int field order, and a message with order 1: nothing is converted, so a caveat's value of another JSON type than its field's is no valid caveat, and no args satisfy it.

name: accept-delegation-in-set
description: A's child to B narrows region in [eu, us] to region in [eu].

name: reject-grant-in-set-widened-child
description: A's child to B has region in [eu, us, apac], a superset instead; the signer refuses it, so it is the real child edited and re-signed with the test log key.

name: accept-delegation-time-bound
description: A's child to B narrows due <= 2026-12-31 to due <= 2026-11-30.

name: reject-grant-time-bound-widened-child
description: A's child to B has due <= 2027-01-31, a later bound instead; the signer refuses it, so it is the real child edited and re-signed with the test log key.

name: accept-unproven-claim-without-evidence
description: A refund.quote with a tests_passed claim and no evidence.

name: accept-unproven-required-claim-missing
description: A refund request under alice's root grant with no claim, though the schema lists approved_by; not strict.
